detailed_findings.finding: Each conjunct in the lemma statement is proved explicitly from the representation n = 1 + 2dt.
The gcd argument is valid: any positive common divisor g of d and n also divides n - 2dt = 1, hence g = 1.
The parity calculation for k(d-dk-2r)/2 is correct via k(d-dk-2r) = -d k(k-1) - 2kr and evenness of k(k-1).

reason: The proof is correct and complete for all stated conclusions. From n ≡ 1 mod 2d it validly writes n = 1 + 2dt, which immediately gives oddness of n and integrality of r(1-n)/2 = -rdt. The argument that any common divisor of d and n must divide 1 correctly proves gcd(d,n)=1. For the final integrality claim, the identity k(d-dk-2r) = -d k(k-1) - 2kr is correct, and both terms are even because k(k-1) is even and 2kr is even, so the half is an integer. The proof matches the lemma sketch and uses only elementary arithmetic with no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
